card.occupation: Float line operator at a glass manufacturing plant, working a four-on, four-off rotating shift pattern of days and nights
card.education_detail: Left a local Catholic high school with GCSEs, including a B in English and a C in Maths. Did a Level 3 BTEC in Engineering at St Helens College, then joined the plant through a manufacturing apprenticeship at 19. Since then he has picked up a Level 2 NVQ in Performing Manufacturing Operations, forklift and overhead crane tickets, and an IOSH Managing Safely certificate the company paid for.
card.household: Lives with his wife Megan, 25, a dental nurse, in a rented two-up two-down terrace in Sutton. They met at sixth-form college and married two years ago at their parish church, with the do at a rugby club function room. No kids yet. They have a rescue greyhound called Dolly and are saving for a deposit to buy somewhere with a proper garden.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in St Helens. Both sides of the family go back generations in the town, with grandparents who worked at the pits and the glassworks. Brought up Catholic. He goes to Mass at Christmas, Easter and the odd Sunday with his mum, and he and Megan married in church. He calls his faith 'quiet but there' and isn't preachy about it. Rugby league is close to a family religion too.
card.professional_persona: Reliable, upbeat operator on the hot end of the float line. He monitors furnace and tin bath readings, checks ribbon thickness and flags defects. He's known for logging everything properly and leaving handovers tidy, which the older lads tease him about. He gets on with everyone from the cleaners to the shift managers and is the one who organises the crew's Christmas night out. He stays calm when there's a line break or a furnace alarm, and the team leader has started leaning on him to show new starters the ropes.
card.sports_persona: St Helens Saints season ticket holder with his dad and younger brother, in the same part of the ground for years. Plays five-a-side on Wednesdays when shifts allow and runs a 5k parkrun at Victoria Park most free Saturdays. He's chasing a sub-21-minute time and keeps a spreadsheet of his splits.
card.arts_persona: Curious more than arty. He's been round the Walker Art Gallery and Tate Liverpool more than once, usually dragging Megan or a mate along. He gets into history and architecture podcasts on the commute and reads non-fiction about engineering, the Industrial Revolution and space. He picked up an old acoustic guitar during lockdown and can manage a few Oasis and Arctic Monkeys songs at parties.
card.travel_persona: Uses the four-off days for cheap trips: Lake District walks, a weekend in Edinburgh, a bus tour of Snowdonia. Honeymooned in Croatia and loved it. He's teaching himself Spanish on Duolingo for a planned trip to Seville and Granada, and he'd rather wander a new city than lie by a pool.
card.culinary_persona: Proper tea is a big deal in their house. He does a decent scouse from his nan's recipe and has got into trying curries and stir-fries from YouTube. On nights he lives on a bacon barm and a flask of tea. Chippy on Fridays if they're both off. He's started batch cooking on Sundays to keep on top of the shifts and the budget.
hobbies_and_interests: St Helens Saints and rugby league generally
Walking Dolly the greyhound round Sherdley Park
Pub quizzes, where he's the team captain at the local on Thursdays
Playing acoustic guitar badly but happily
DIY around the rented house within what the landlord allows
skills: Float glass line operation and quality checks
card.career_goals: Wants to make shift team leader in the next couple of years, then maybe move into a process technician or health and safety role. He has looked into the company sponsoring an HNC in manufacturing engineering. He wants something steady enough for a mortgage and kids, and he admits he'd get bored doing exactly the same job forever.
card.voice: Chatty, warm and quick, with a St Helens accent that sits somewhere between Scouse and Wigan, though not heavy. He talks fast when he's enthused and slows down when he's explaining something technical. He says 'erm' when picking his words, and uses 'sort of' and 'to be fair' a lot, plus the odd 'do you know what I mean'. Says 'tea' for the evening meal, 'barm' for a roll and 'give it me', and occasionally 'yous' to a group. He says 'me mum' and calls people 'mate'. He's comfortable with silence on a call, but he usually fills it with a joke or a 'sorry, go on' if he's talked over someone. He echoes questions back while he thinks: 'what would I change? erm...'
card.typing: Quick but fairly tidy. He capitalises the first word and usually ends with a full stop, but he drops apostrophes when rushing ('dont', 'im', 'its'). He uses 'n' for 'and' now and then, adds the occasional 'tbh' or 'lol', and spells everything right because he hates looking sloppy. Answers are short and to the point, sometimes with an extra sentence of detail he couldn't resist adding.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and easy to talk to, the sort who asks you where you're from within two minutes and finds something in common. He's confident without being cocky, laughs easily and doesn't get flustered by odd questions. He's genuinely curious about other people's jobs and will ask follow-up questions. He's honest and straightforward, though he won't overshare about money or his marriage with someone he's just met.
small_things: Being knackered after a run of night shifts
Saints' latest result or a dodgy refereeing call
Dolly the greyhound being scared of the hoover
A podcast he's just listened to about the Titanic or the Moon landings
Megan making him watch Love Island
The price of petrol for the drive to work
Getting a bacon barm from the van outside the plant
deeper_things: Feeling pressure to buy a house and start a family while rents keep going up
His grandad's lung problems from the pits, and why he takes safety so seriously
Occasionally wondering if he should have gone to university, given how much he likes learning
His faith being something he keeps privately but values, especially after his nan died last year
Worrying about automation at the plant, even though he tries to stay positive
Wanting to be a better dad than some of the lads he grew up around had
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at chest height, angled slightly upward, in a small back bedroom used as a box room. It's daytime, and soft light comes from a window off to the left, so the left side of his face is brighter. A young white man with a broad, friendly face, light stubble and blue-grey eyes, mid-laugh with a wide open grin. His short light-brown hair is faded at the sides and slightly longer and messy on top. No glasses. He's wearing a navy St Helens Saints training top with the zip half down. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed wedding photo slightly off-centre, a cheap white flat-pack shelf holding a few paperbacks, a parkrun finisher token on a lanyard and a small wooden crucifix. An acoustic guitar leans against the wall in the right-hand corner. The edge of a clothes airer with work hi-vis trousers on it is just in frame at the bottom right.
